executiveSummary: On September 5, 2026, a HIGH severity incident was detected: "Access Control Vendor Ransomware Incident". The incident involved SecureAccess Solutions (Physical Access Control System Provider), affecting 4 service(s). Over 1 hour 12 minutes, the response team made 3 documented decisions (1 CONTINUE, 1 DEGRADE, 1 PAUSE). The team tracked 5 facts, 3 assumptions, and 4 unknowns. Current status: MONITORING.

keyDecisions.title: Pause automated provisioning
keyDecisions.description: Halt all automated badge provisioning until vendor provides all-clear
keyDecisions.rationale: Cannot verify integrity of new credentials being created; conservative posture until vendor confirms no data tampering
assumptionsMade: Vendor ransomware did not compromise credential database
keyDecisions.reviewTrigger: Vendor confirms no compromise of credential database

keyDecisions.title: Implement manual visitor check-in
keyDecisions.description: Switch to paper-based visitor management at all locations
keyDecisions.rationale: Visitor management integration with vendor system cannot be verified; manual process ensures security while maintaining operations
assumptionsMade: Paper-based process is sufficient for current volume

lessonsLearned: Vendor ransomware notification came through non-emergency channel, causing 15-minute delay
Mobile credential app failure created confusion at locations relying heavily on mobile credentials
Paper visitor management procedures were outdated at 3 locations
GSOC team demonstrated strong decision documentation discipline throughout incident
recommendations: Establish dedicated emergency notification channel with critical vendors
Maintain backup physical credential issuance capability at all locations with significant mobile credential usage
Conduct quarterly review and drill of manual backup procedures at all locations
Add vendor ransomware response scenario to annual GSOC training curriculum
Review vendor contract SLA for incident notification requirements
